items.stem:
A 45-year-old man in Ranchi has very high fasting blood glucose; his urine shows glucose and ketone bodies.
(i) Name the disorder. (1 mark)
(ii) Which hormone and which cells are involved? (1 mark)
(iii) Explain how this hormone normally lowers blood glucose. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Diabetes mellitus. (ii) Insulin; β-cells of the islets of Langerhans. (iii) Insulin acts on hepatocytes and adipocytes, enhancing cellular glucose uptake and utilisation and stimulating conversion of glucose to glycogen (glycogenesis).

items.stem:

(b) A hormone has these effects: regulates the 24-hour diurnal rhythm. Identify the hormone – thyroid hormones or melatonin? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Thyroid hormones: regulate the basal metabolic rate; support RBC formation; control metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats. Melatonin: secreted by the pineal gland; regulates the 24-hour diurnal rhythm; maintains normal sleep-wake cycle. (b) Melatonin.

items.stem: Explain the mechanism of hormone action through membrane-bound and intracellular receptors with diagrams. Classify hormones by chemical nature.

items.answer: Steroid hormones and iodothyronines interact mostly with intracellular receptors.
items.markingKey: (b) Steroid hormones and iodothyronines interact mostly with intracellular receptors. The other statements are false. Protein hormones bind to membrane-bound receptors and act through second messengers. Steroid hormones interact mostly with intracellular receptors and regulate gene expression. Adrenaline and noradrenaline are amino-acid derivatives.
options: Steroid hormones always act through second messengers.
Steroid hormones and iodothyronines interact mostly with intracellular receptors.
Protein hormones enter the cell and bind to nuclear receptors.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “ANF increases blood pressure.”
items.answer: ANF dilates blood vessels and reduces blood pressure.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: ANF dilates blood vessels and reduces blood pressure.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3) are secreted by the thyroid follicles.
Reason (R): Oxytocin is produced by the posterior pituitary.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Oxytocin is synthesised by the hypothalamus and stored and released by the neurohypophysis.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: What is meant by “hormone receptors”?
items.answer: Specific proteins, located in the target tissues only, to which hormones bind to produce their effects.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: specific proteins, located in the target tissues only, to which hormones bind to produce their effects.

items.stem:
A hormone has these effects: maintains normal sleep-wake cycle; regulates the 24-hour diurnal rhythm; influences body temperature and metabolism.
(i) Identify the hormone. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were growth hormone? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Melatonin (ii) secreted by the pineal gland (iii) deficiency in childhood causes pituitary dwarfism; stimulates body growth
items.markingKey: (i) melatonin – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: secreted by the pineal gland – 1 mark. (iii) for growth hormone: secreted by the adenohypophysis; stimulates body growth; over-secretion causes gigantism – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Protein hormones enter the cell and bind to nuclear receptors.”
items.answer: Protein hormones bind to membrane-bound receptors and act through second messengers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Protein hormones bind to membrane-bound receptors and act through second messengers.

items.stem: Which of the following is a hormone of the heart or kidney?
items.answer: atrial natriuretic factor
items.markingKey: (a) Atrial natriuretic factor is a hormone of the heart or kidney; the others are not.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between melatonin and glucagon on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A hormone has these effects: secreted by α-cells of the islets of Langerhans. Identify the hormone – melatonin or glucagon? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Melatonin: secreted by the pineal gland; regulates the 24-hour diurnal rhythm; maintains normal sleep-wake cycle. Glucagon: secreted by α-cells of the islets of Langerhans; hyperglycaemic; stimulates glycogenolysis. (b) Glucagon.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: glucagon; 1 mark: “secreted by α-cells of the islets of Langerhans” is a feature of glucagon.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Insulin increases blood glucose levels.”
items.answer: Insulin is hypoglycaemic; glucagon raises blood glucose.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Insulin is hypoglycaemic; glucagon raises blood glucose.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a peptide, polypeptide or protein hormone?
items.answer: cortisol
items.markingKey: (b) Cortisol is a steroid hormone, not a peptide, polypeptide or protein hormone.

items.stem: A hormone has these effects: secreted by the adrenal medulla; increases heart beat and rate of respiration; increases alertness, pupil dilation and piloerection. Identify the hormone. Give a reason.
items.answer: Adrenaline
items.markingKey: 1 mark: adrenaline; 1 mark: the features secreted by the adrenal medulla; increases heart beat and rate of respiration; increases alertness, pupil dilation and piloerection are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
A hormone from a non-endocrine organ is described: stimulates erythropoiesis; a peptide hormone; increases RBC formation.
(i) Identify the hormone. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were secretin? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Erythropoietin (ii) secreted by juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney (iii) stimulates secretion of water; gastrointestinal hormone
items.markingKey: (i) erythropoietin – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: secreted by juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney – 1 mark. (iii) for secretin: gastrointestinal hormone; acts on the exocrine pancreas; stimulates secretion of water – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Define the term “gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP)”.
items.answer: A hormone that inhibits gastric secretion and motility.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a hormone that inhibits gastric secretion and motility.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a disorder due to hypersecretion?
items.answer: cretinism
items.markingKey: (d) Cretinism is a disorder due to hyposecretion, not a disorder due to hypersecretion.

items.stem: A mode of hormone action is described: generates second messengers such as cAMP; used by protein hormones like FSH. Identify the type of receptor involved. Give a reason.
items.answer: A membrane-bound receptor
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a membrane-bound receptor; 1 mark: the features generates second messengers such as cAMP; used by protein hormones like FSH are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following is an amino-acid derivative hormone?
items.answer: adrenaline
items.markingKey: (b) Adrenaline is an amino-acid derivative hormone; the others are not.

items.stem: A hormone from a non-endocrine organ is described: gastrointestinal hormone; stimulates secretion of water. Identify the hormone.
items.answer: secretin
items.markingKey: (a) Secretin: gastrointestinal hormone; stimulates secretion of water.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between gastrin and erythropoietin on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A hormone from a non-endocrine organ is described: stimulates erythropoiesis. Identify the hormone – gastrin or erythropoietin? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Gastrin: gastrointestinal hormone; acts on gastric glands; stimulates secretion of HCl. Erythropoietin: secreted by juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney; stimulates erythropoiesis; increases RBC formation. (b) Erythropoietin.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: erythropoietin; 1 mark: “stimulates erythropoiesis” is a feature of erythropoietin.

items.stem: What is meant by “gigantism”?
items.answer: Abnormal growth of the body leading to great height due to over-secretion of growth hormone.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: abnormal growth of the body leading to great height due to over-secretion of growth hormone.

items.stem: Give two differences between an intracellular receptor and a membrane-bound receptor.
items.answer: An intracellular receptor: hormone enters the cell; used by steroid hormones and iodothyronines. A membrane-bound receptor: hormone does not enter the cell; used by protein hormones like FSH.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. an intracellular receptor – hormone enters the cell; used by steroid hormones and iodothyronines; a membrane-bound receptor – hormone does not enter the cell; used by protein hormones like FSH.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the mechanism of hormone action is correct?
items.answer: Hormones interacting with intracellular receptors regulate gene expression or chromosome function.
items.markingKey: (d) Hormones interacting with intracellular receptors regulate gene expression or chromosome function. The other statements are false. Protein hormones bind to membrane-bound receptors and act through second messengers. Steroid hormones interact mostly with intracellular receptors and regulate gene expression. Adrenaline and noradrenaline are amino-acid derivatives.
options: Steroid hormones always act through second messengers.
Protein hormones enter the cell and bind to nuclear receptors.
Hormones interacting with intracellular receptors regulate gene expression or chromosome function.
